subject: MSA: Liability cap approach — fees multiple vs annual bucket
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Perez <maria.perez@datapulse.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MSA redlines: Liability cap — initial ask

Maria / Contracts team,

Thanks for sending over the redlined MSA. Monica and I reviewed the liability section and wanted to outline a couple of scenarios we think balance commercial risk and your need for recovery options. High level: we can propose either a single aggregate cap tied to the total fees paid in the Term, or an annualized cap that resets each 12-month period.

Option A (aggregate cap): greater of $1.5M or 3x fees paid in the Contract Term.
Option B (annualized cap): greater of $750k per 12-month period or 2x annual fees.

We also recommend clarifying carve-outs: (1) willful misconduct and gross negligence remain excluded, (2) fidelity of data / regulatory fines — propose disagreement language: capped at damages actually paid to third parties, except in cases of unauthorized data disclosure where we accept a narrow carve-out up to $2M for remediation.

Can you confirm which approach Datapulse prefers? If you have internal constraints (procurement/legal preferred cap floors or multiples), share them and we’ll iterate.

I’ve attached our annotated MSA for reference (MSA_redlines_Datapulse_v2.pdf).

Thanks,
Jordan
Sr. Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.ai]
[Attachment: MSA_redlines_Datapulse_v2.pdf]

From: Maria Perez <maria.perez@datapulse.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Contracts <contracts@datapulse.ai>
Date: 2026-10-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines: Liability cap — initial ask

Jordan — appreciate the clear options. Quick feedback from our side:

- Datapulse procurement leans toward an annualized approach because our budgeting operates on fiscal-year buckets. An annual reset is non-starter unless the floor is high enough.
- Legal is wary of carve-outs that permit uncapped recovery for data breaches. They may accept a higher capped remedy but not uncapped exposure.

Can you send us the rationale behind the multiple choices (3x vs 2x) in a single paragraph? Our counsel wants to see a short justification to take to the VP of Finance.

I'll loop Erik (security) if we need to discuss the data-loss remediation cap.

Best,
Maria
Contracts Manager, Datapulse
[maria.perez@datapulse.ai]

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-18T12:15:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: MSA redlines: Liability cap — initial ask

Jordan / Karthik — forwarding Maria's note. Maria asked for a concise rationale for multiples. Draft below, please edit: 

- Commercial rationale: multiples of fees align the counterparty’s recovery with the financial scale of the engagement; higher multiples (3x) reflect business-critical integrations and our operational exposure for heavier custom work. Lower multiples (2x) are typical for plug-and-play SaaS with standard SLAs.

Karthik, any legal framing we should add (e.g., reference to market norms or case law)?

Monica
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: OrderForm-ExhibitA.xlsx]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-19T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: MSA redlines: Liability cap — initial ask

Monica / Jordan — suggested short rationale for Maria / Datapulse legal: 

"We propose a fee-multiple cap to proportionally limit exposure relative to the economic value of the engagement. A 3x multiple for aggregate caps is proposed where engagements involve dedicated engineering commitment, custom integration, or sensitive data handling, reflecting higher operational and remediation costs. A 2x multiple for annualized caps is proposed for standard-hosted deployments with limited customization. Both figures are within market ranges for enterprise SaaS vendors and allow customers meaningful recovery while keeping vendor liability insurable and predictable."

On carve-outs: recommend carving out (1) claims for indemnified third-party IP infringement, (2) claims resulting from willful misconduct/gross negligence (standard), and (3) statutory fines where applicable but with a specific cap for regulatory penalties tied to the nature of the breach (e.g., data exposure remediation capped at $2M).

If Datapulse insists on an annual reset, propose the annualized floor be increased to $1M or 2x annual fees (whichever is greater) to mitigate per-year erosion of risk allocation.

I'll draft redline language for both options and upload today.

Karthik
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Maria Perez <maria.perez@datapulse.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Contracts <contracts@datapulse.ai>, Erik Johnson <erik.j@datapulse.ai>
Date: 2026-10-20T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines: Liability cap — initial ask

Thanks — that language helps. Quick answers from our side after internal sync: 

- Datapulse prefers the annualized approach but will consider an aggregate cap if Redwood can accept the annual floor of $1M (or 2x annual fees, whichever is higher).
- On the data exposure carve-out: Security will not accept uncapped liability. They are open to a specific higher cap tied to remediation and monitoring costs (we discussed $2M as a reference). If Redwood is willing to commit to enhanced incident response timelines (RTO/RPO obligations + crediting for forensic support), we can accept the $2M capped remedy.

Next steps: Karthik, can you provide the two redline snippets (Option A aggregate; Option B annualized with $1M floor) plus a short incident response SLA clause to slot into Section 7? If we get those, Contracts will do a side-by-side and aim to respond by week’s end.

Appreciate the collaboration.

Maria
Contracts Manager, Datapulse
[Attachment: none]
